newsitem.title: UK: OPEC Jan output up 300,000 bpd to 26.64 mln - survey.
newsitem.headline: OPEC Jan output up 300,000 bpd to 26.64 mln - survey.

text.p: OPEC output hit a new 16-year high in January, swollen by Iraq's first full month of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange.

Wellhead crude oil production from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries rose 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.64 million in January from a revised 26.34 million in December, a Reuter survey of oil analysts, OPEC delegates and company officials found.

And OPEC, pumping an extra 600,000 bpd in the past two months, looks set to add more barrels as foreign companies, bringing new fields onstream, seek to cash in on their investments, OPEC monitors said.
"I see OPEC heading to 27 million bpd by the middle of the year -- easily," said Mehdi Varzi, director of research for energy at finance house Kleinwort Benson Securities.
OPEC's official output ceiling is a combined 25.033 million bpd for the 11-member cartel.
Iraq's output, boosted by some 500,000 bpd of exports, rose 190,000 bpd to 1.12 million in January, the survey found.
Baghdad has found no difficulty in selling its crude after quickly wrapping up some 25 contracts with buyers from Asia, Europe and the United States.
Most OPEC countries continued to ignore official output quotas leaving rising demand to absorb extra supplies without any adverse impact on prices.
January saw small rises from Nigeria and Qatar for the third month in succession as new foreign company operated fields build toward full capacity.
Nigeria was pegged at 2.1 million bpd, 235,000 bpd over quota, aided by rising supplies from two long-term joint-venture producers Mobil and Chevron and a newcomer, Canada's Abacan.
Qatar pumped 550,000 bpd, or 163,000 bpd over quota, with the help of the new Arco operated Al-Rayyan field.

Even the United Arab Emirates appeared to stretch output in January. The UAE is one of only a trio of core Middle East producers, with OPEC kingpin Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, seen holding any spare capacity.
But monitors saw 2.25 million bpd from the UAE in January some 90,000 bpd in excess of its official allocation.

Saudi Arabia maintained output at quota in January, running at 8.01 million bpd. A Gulf source said state company Aramco turned down requests for extra volumes from buyers looking for incremental supplies permitted under Saudi term contracts.
"We could supply even more than we are producing right now," said the Gulf source. "The Gulf states have had to turn down customer requests for more oil."
With more than two million bpd of capacity in mothballs, Saudi policy will remain key to the fortunes of the oil markets this year.
But there is no sign from the Kingdom that it intends to dip into its spare capacity reserve.
"Having enjoyed the fruits of restraint in the oil price rise of 1996 I think they'll be loathe to jeopardise similar returns in 1997," said Kleinwort's Varzi.
Venezuela kept volumes running high, at 3.17 million in January, hugely in excess of its 2.36 million bpd quota.
Monitors said state company PdVSA spiked crude exports with condensate in January because condensate prices in the U.S. Gulf were not high enough to warrant separate sales.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
